newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed but holds range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed but holds range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended narrowly mixed Friday in a lackluster session, but a relatively steady cash market ensured prices remained in recent technical ranges, industry sources said.
April climbed 1.8 cents to close at $1.96 per million British thermal units. May settled 0.4 cent higher at $2.021. Other deferreds ended on either side of unchanged.

"We're stuck again in a range. There's been some weather and injection demand to support it, but without the weather, you're going to be pressed to find some bullish news," said one Midwest trader, adding he expected May to be pressured.
NYMEX April Hub natgas expires on Monday, March 24.

While producer region injections and cool Northeast weather should underpin physical and paper prices early next week, few expected much upside, with overall stocks in good shape and typically-weak spring demand just around the corner. Technical traders still pegged resistance in April at $2.04, then in the mid-teens and at $2.28. Support was seen at the nine-day moving average of $1.925, then at $1.88, $1.78-1.80 and the $1.701 contract low.
Most chartists agreed it would take a close above $2.04 or below $1.88 to trigger some momentum.

In the cash Friday, Gulf Coast weekend prices were steady to down slightly in the low-to-mid $1.90s. Midcon pipes were a couple of cents lower in the high-$1.80s. Colder Northeast weather firmed New York city prices slightly to about $2.30.
The 12-month strip gained 0.4 cent to $2.115. NYMEX said an estimated 17,338 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 27,408.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Friday.
On the KCBT, April finished 2.1 cents higher at $1.74, while deferreds ended up by one-half to 2.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.3 cent to 22.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
